results.name: Dumbbell Plank Pullthrough
instructions: Begin in a high plank with your hands directly below your shoulders, your feet slightly apart, and a dumbbell positioned on the floor beside one hand.
Shift your weight onto one hand and reach your opposite hand underneath your torso to grasp the dumbbell.
Drag the dumbbell across the floor to the opposite side while keeping your shoulders and hips facing the floor.
Place your hand back on the floor, repeat the pull with the opposite arm, and continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your torso as you reach underneath.
Transfer your weight smoothly without collapsing into your supporting shoulder.
Drag the dumbbell across the floor instead of lifting it upward.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell across and inhale as you return your hand to the floor.
results.description: Dumbbell Plank Pullthrough is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Chest, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, allowing your arms to hang below your shoulders.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and raise both dumbbells backward by extending your arms behind your hips.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the backs of your shoulders while keeping your torso still.
Slowly lower the dumbbells until they hang below your shoulders, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the bend in your elbows fixed without turning the exercise into a row.
Move your arms backward from your shoulders rather than swinging the dumbbells.
Keep your torso still and avoid rising as you lift the weights.
Exhale as you raise the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Shoulder Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Silverback Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand using an overhand grip. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward while keeping your back straight and your arms hanging below your shoulders.
Keep your elbows straight and raise both shoulders toward your ears, allowing the dumbbells to move slightly upward.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back without lifting your torso.
Slowly lower your shoulders until your arms hang fully extended, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows straight and avoid rowing or curling the weights.
Allow your shoulders to lower fully between repetitions without rounding your spine.
Keep your knees slightly bent and maintain the same hip-hinge position.
Exhale as you raise your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Upright Row
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in front of your thigh using an overhand grip. Keep your free arm relaxed by your side.
Pull the dumbbell upward close to your torso by leading with your elbow and moving it outward and upward.
Raise the dumbbell toward your upper chest until your elbow is higher than your wrist.
Slowly lower the dumbbell along the same path until your arm is fully extended, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Lead the pull with your elbow rather than lifting with your hand.
Avoid using momentum or shrugging excessively to lift the weight.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning backward as the dumbbell rises.
Exhale as you raise the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Single Arm Upright Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Elevated Pike Shoulder Shrug
instructions: Place the balls of both feet on an elevated platform and position your hands shoulder width apart on the floor. Straighten your arms and legs, then lift your hips until your body forms an inverted V shape.
Keep your elbows fixed with a slight bend, lowering your upper body slightly between your arms.
Press firmly through your palms and shrug your shoulders upwards, raising your upper body without bending your elbows.
Lower your shoulders with control to return to the starting position, then repeat while keeping your feet fixed and your hips elevated.
tips: Keep your hands shoulder width apart and spread your fingers for stability.
Keep your elbows fixed with a slight bend so the movement occurs through your shoulder blades.
Keep your legs extended and the balls of your feet firmly supported on the platform.
Exhale as you shrug your shoulders upward and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Elevated Pike Shoulder Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core, Forearms.

results.name: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Alternate Arms
instructions: Sit on the Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press machine, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward.
Press one handle upward by extending your arm fully while keeping the other arm stationary.
Squeeze your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement and slowly return the handle to the starting position with control.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handle upward and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
results.description: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Alternate Arms is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Both Arms
instructions: Sit on the Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press machine, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward.
Press both handles upward by extending your arms fully with control.
Squeeze your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement and slowly return the handles to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handles upward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Both Arms is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Single Arm
instructions: Sit on the Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press machine, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward.
Press the right handle upward by extending your arm fully while keeping the other arm stationary.
Squeeze your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement and slowly return the handle to the starting position with control.
Repeat with the same arm for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handle upward and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
results.description: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Single Arm is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Jump Rope Face Pull
instructions: Loop the jump rope over a vertical bar or similar stable structure, ensuring the rope is at about hip height. Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles of the jump rope with both hands.
Step back slightly to create tension in the rope, keeping your core engaged and your back straight.
Pull the rope towards your face by bending your elbows and bringing your hands towards your ears, engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles.
Extend your arms back out to the starting position with control. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together as you pull the rope towards your face to maximize muscle engagement.
Move slowly with control and avoid using momentum to prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the rope towards your face and inhaling as you extend your arms back out.
Ensure the vertical bar or structure is stable and can support the tension in the rope to prevent slipping or injury.
results.description: Jump Rope Face Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Kettlebell Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell by the handle with both hands in front of you, keeping your arms extended.
Raise the kettlebell forward and upward, keeping your elbows straight as you are lifting the weight.
Continue lifting until your hands reach about chin height and your elbows are near shoulder height.
Lower the kettlebell along the same path until your arms are extended, then repeat.
tips: Maintain an upright torso throughout the exercise.
Avoid leaning backward to lift the kettlebell higher.
Raise and lower the weight smoothly without using momentum.
Exhale as you raise the kettlebell and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Kettlebell Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.
